transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-08-27
Time: 15:00 PT
Duration: 52 minutes
Attendees: Emma Li (Redwood AE), Daniel Park (Redwood SE), Mark Johnson (CISO, Silver Creek), Sara Patel (Head of Cloud Ops), Luis Ramirez (CTO)
---
Summary (auto): Quick discovery on data residency and compliance needs. Customer evaluating Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private for EU/US data residency and HIPAA/financial controls. Requested SOC2/HIPAA docs, network diagram, and EU benchmark run. Next: send security pack, schedule deep-dive and PoC benchmarking window.
---
[00:00] Emma: hey everyone thanks for joining, i'll kick off, i'm emma from redwood, and with me is daniel our se. um, can we do quick intros from your side?
[00:12] Mark: yeah i'm mark, chief information security officer at silver creek bank, we've got regulatory constraints, payment card and personal data, so data residency is critical.
[00:20] Sara: sara here, head of cloud ops, we manage our infra across aws and a private dc in frankfurt, so region specifics matter.
[00:27] Luis: luis, cto, i'm focused on the architecture and latency trade-offs.
[00:33] Emma: great, high level agenda: understand current stack, data flows, compliance must-haves (gdpr/hipaa/financial rules), and rough timeline and success criteria.
[00:44] Daniel: i'll also cover network/topology, logging, and how our dedicated/private options work from a technical perspective.
[00:50] Mark: perfect. first question - are you able to guarantee that data for eu customers stays in eu? like physically.
[00:58] Emma: yes, sort of - for hosted we have region pins; we can route requests to eu-hosted infra. for guaranteed isolation we typically recommend Dedicated or Private where you get tenant isolation and can choose eu-only hosting. note there are also contract-level addenda for data processing.
[01:18] Sara: can you explain difference, like what's the difference between hosted eu and dedicated in practice?
[01:25] Daniel: sure. hosted eu is our multi-tenant hosted api with eu regions only, we do logical separation but it's still shared infra. dedicated allocates reserved gpu pools and provides network isolation within the region, and private is full control plane in your vpc or on-prem. dedicated gives you more predictable throughput and stronger data separation.
[01:46] Mark: for auditors we need proof that logs containing pii are not exported offsite. what does redwood log and where is it retained?
[01:55] Daniel: good question. we capture operational telemetry, request metadata, and optional request/response logs. for hosted multi-tenant, request logs can be stored in-region but default retention is 30 days; we can provide redaction and short retention, and we offer options to disable request logging entirely for sensitive workloads. for dedicated/private customers, you control log routing and retention, and we support pushing logs to your splunk/cloudwatch or to an s3 bucket in your account.
[02:24] Sara: can you confirm we can disable logging of full request payloads? auditors don't allow storing full PII.
[02:31] Daniel: yes, you can disable full payload logging. additionally we have automatic pii redaction hooks and guide on scrubbers. across private deployments, logs never leave your VPC unless you point them out.
[02:43] Mark: encryption questions - KMS, HSM, keys managed by us?
[02:47] Emma: we support customer-managed keys for dedicated and private via KMS (aws kms) and HSM integrations; for hosted we use provider-managed keys but can do CMKs under enterprise contracts.
[02:59] Luis: about latency - if we host in eu region, how different is performance between hosted and dedicated? we need 95th < 400ms for our interactive support flows.
[03:09] Daniel: dedicated typically gives you tighter p95 due to reserved GPUs and predictable batching; hosted multi-tenant has more variance but is often acceptable. we can run a benchmark with your payloads in eu to measure. note that sequence length and model quantization change latencies.
[03:26] Mark: GDPR-specific: can customers exercise right to be forgotten? if a user requests deletion, how do you ensure derivatives from models aren't retained?
[03:35] Emma: we provide data deletion endpoints and support data subject requests; for hosted we maintain DPA controls and can delete stored logs and associated artifacts. for learned model weights, we're not training on customer inputs by default; we isolate logs and do not fine-tune shared models with customer data unless explicitly engaged. i will confirm the exact wording for gdpr DSRs in the pack.
[03:58] Sara: regulatory asks around audit logs - we need immutable audit trails for admin actions, sso changes, model rollouts. do you provide that?
[04:06] Daniel: yes, we surface admin audit logs, they can be exported to your syslog or s3 and are immutable with retention policies. in private deployments you control the audit store.
[04:17] Mark: HIPAA - we have advisors saying anything with PHI must be covered by a bpa/baa. do you support HIPAA and sign BAAs?
[04:25] Emma: we support HIPAA-covered deployments. we have customers running PHI workloads on dedicated/private. we can provide the legal BAA and compliance docs during contracting. i'll include our HIPAA scoping in the package.
[04:36] Luis: specific to financial services, do you have support for restricted logging where transaction traces must be obfuscated?
[04:43] Daniel: yes, we support field-level redaction and tokenization before logging; you can supply a scrubber lambda or use our built-in redaction rules. we also support masking in the response logs.
[04:55] Sara: network/security - if we go dedicated in aws eu-central, do you support VPC endpoints, private link, and no public egress?
[05:03] Daniel: yes, we support VPC peering, VPC endpoints, and PrivateLink-like setups for Dedicated and Private. for hosted, you can restrict ingress via IP allowlists but it's more limited.
[05:14] Mark: how about data retention windows - auditors want 90 days for some logs and 7 years for transaction backups; can retention be configured per-log-type?
[05:23] Emma: yes, retention policies are configurable per log type in Dedicated/Private. hosted has preset tiers but we can negotiate enterprise retention SLAs. we'll capture your retention matrix in the follow-up.
[05:35] Luis: timeline - we're aiming for a pilot in q4, production in q2 next year. what are lead times for dedicated and private?
[05:42] Emma: Dedicated reservations can be provisioned in a few weeks once contract signed, Private on-prem or VPC deployments typically take 6-10 weeks depending on network approvals and air-gap requirements. we'll include estimated timelines in the pricing doc.
[05:57] Sara: sample data - can you run a benchmark using our sample dataset within eu region? we need to see tokenization/latency and cost estimates.
[06:05] Daniel: absolutely, we'll schedule a benchmark. we'll need a sanitized sample and an approximate QPS/sequence length profile.
[06:12] Mark: about contracts - is there a clause for data residency breach penalties? auditors insist on contractual liability if logs are mishandled.
[06:21] Emma: we have standard DPAs and can include residency addenda; commercial/legal will work with you on liability clauses.
[06:28] Speaker 4: (inaudible) quick question on model variants - can you lock to older model versions?
[06:33] Daniel: yes, customers can pin model versions for rollouts and we support canary and automatic fallback policies.
[06:39] Mark: do you perform any downstream indexing that could rebuild PII? like vector indexes?
[06:44] Daniel: vector indexes are not built on customer inputs unless enabled; for Hosted we have optional embeddings pipelines but these can be disabled or run into your account. we'll document default behaviors.
[06:56] Sara: ok auditors will also want SSO/SAML integration and RBAC scoping so only certain users can see logs.
[07:03] Emma: yes we support SSO (SAML/OIDC), role-based access controls and per-route permissioning. we'll share doc links.
[07:12] Luis: cost - what's the delta between hosted eu and dedicated? general rough numbers?
[07:18] Emma: hosted is lowest entry cost but higher unit variance; dedicated has a reservation-based model with lower per-token costs at scale; private has higher setup fees but best isolation. i'll include ballpark pricing tiers.
[07:30] Mark: what about deletion guarantees for backups? backups sometimes replicate across regions for disaster recovery. our auditors won't accept cross-region replication for eu-only datasets.
[07:40] Daniel: for dedicated/private we can configure backup targets to be region-local only; for hosted we need to confirm per-case, but enterprise contracts can specify no cross-region replication.
[07:52] Sara: any certifications we should know? soc2 type ii, iso27001?
[07:56] Emma: yes, we have SOC2 Type II and we're ISO27001 certified; we'll include certificate copies.
[08:04] Mark: great. one last thing - can you do penetration testing or provide results?
[08:09] Daniel: we do annual third-party pentests and can share summary reports under NDA.
[08:15] Emma: ok let's recap next steps: i'll send the security pack (SOC2, HIPAA scoping, network guide) and pricing, daniel will schedule a technical deep-dive and benchmark in the eu region, and sara will share a sanitized sample dataset and retention matrix.
[08:32] Mark: perfect. target for pilot kickoff meeting - week of 2026-10-12.
[08:37] Emma: sounds good. thanks all, we'll follow up via email with calendars and links.
[08:41] Luis: thanks.
[08:43] (call ends)
